26:29 The changing role of software engineers
29:25 Microsoft’s voluntary exit offers
34:05 AI anxiety and changing roles
36:35 Junior hiring

45:39 Owning your AI infrastructure
51:21 Building trust in AI agents
53:48 Local models and hybrid intelligence
56:39 Microsoft’s model strategy
59:26 Advice for engineers
1:01:21 Closing takeaways

Brought to you by:

• @turbopuffer  – a vector and full-text search engine built on object storage. It’s fast, cheap, and extremely scalable. https://t.co/w9y67Gs8ab (I built a greatly improved podcast/newseltter search with it, check it out: https://t.co/6zbxlEaHlu)

• @linear  – the product development system for teams and agents. https://t.co/knIF2mcz9p

• @WorkOS  – everything you need to make your app enterprise-ready. https://t.co/aiAee0oF5h

3 interesting takeaways from Satya:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work. 

Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

2. “Own the intelligence”: avoid lock-in & treat agents as an insider risk. 

Satya cautions companies to avoid lock-in with any single model provider by ensuring that the harness, memory, and model are not coupled, so that they can be changed with ease. He also thinks more companies should consider using open models as a way to protect their core intellectual property (IP) from leaking out, and build private evals to decide what models to use and upgrade to. He also says that models are intelligent but unreliable, so it’s best to treat them as “insider risks” and build a separate system to verify that agentic systems work as expected.

3. What’s with those voluntary exit offers? 

I asked Satya directly why Microsoft recently made voluntary exit offers to most of its software engineers for the first time in the company’s history. I also wanted to know if it could mean layoffs in the future. Unsurprisingly, his reply was diplomatic, but in the podcast I rehashed what I heard in a more direct way.

53:48 本地模型和混合智能
56:39 微软的模型策略
59:26 给工程师的建议
1:01:21 结束要点

为您带来：

• @turbopuffer – 基于对象存储构建的矢量和全文搜索引擎。它快速、便宜且可扩展性极强。 （我用它构建了一个大大改进的播客/新闻搜索，请查看：）

• @ Linear – 团队和代理的产品开发系统。

• @WorkOS – 让您的应用程序为企业做好准备所需的一切。

Satya 的 3 个有趣要点：

1. 一种新的软件工程形式：团队构建软件工厂来改进他们的工作。

Satya 引用了 Azure 网络团队的例子，该团队管理着 500 多家光纤网络运营商，并且最近构建了一个代理系统来更好地管理电子邮件和流程。现在，他们的运营效率大大提高了。 Satya 认为这是“人工智能转型”的现实：棕地致力于建设软件工厂，以改善团队的运作方式，同时继续日常工作。

2.“拥有情报”：避免锁定并将代理视为内部风险。

Satya 警告公司要避免与任何单一模型提供商锁定，确保线束、内存和模型不耦合，以便可以轻松更改。他还认为更多的公司应该考虑使用开放模型来保护其核心知识产权（IP）免遭泄露，并建立私人评估来决定使用和升级到哪些模型。他还表示，模型是智能的，但不可靠，因此最好将它们视为“内部风险”，并构建一个单独的系统来验证代理系统是否按预期工作。

3. 这些自愿退出要约是怎么回事？

我直接问萨提亚，为什么微软最近向大多数软件工程师提出了自愿退出的提议，这在公司历史上还是第一次。我还想知道这是否意味着将来会裁员。不出所料，他的回答很外交，但在播客中我以更直接的方式重申了我听到的内容。

US to invade Iran before Dec 31st 2027? What will the reaction be with oil markets?

Oil Market:

Clara Lin:
"Oil swings hit my budget, but ngl the Iran risk has me tempted. I’m small leveraged long crude for now, and I’ll add if prices start jumping."

The General:
"My household can absorb some volatility, but I’m not letting Iran headlines catch me flat-footed. I’ve added oil exposure in stages; markets move before the cha…"

if a buyer finds an agent that can do the job, what happens next?

on https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB, TermiX's AI agent marketp
title_en:
if a buyer finds an agent that can do the job, what happens next?

on https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB, TermiX's AI agent marketplace, discovery is only the first step toward a transaction

a listing helps people discover what an agent offers, how much it costs, and how long delivery might take

that's an important starting point, but finding a service doesn't automatically create a transaction

a provider can publish a listing and wait for buyers to discover the service. or a buyer can publish a request describing the work, budget, scope, and requirements, allowing providers to find that opportunity and submit quotes

both paths can lead to the same commerce workflow: Offer, Checkout, and Order

for example, imagine a buyer needs an agent to write landing page content. they could browse existing listings and choose a provider, or publish a request describing the exact work and budget they have in mind

once both sides find a suitable match, they can agree on the scope, price, delivery time, and other terms through an Offer

then comes Checkout, where the buyer funds the order through escrow. after that, the provider still needs to accept the funded Order onchain before starting the work

and the process doesn't end when the agent delivers the result. the buyer can review the delivery, request a redo, or challenge it before the order reaches settlement

to me, a useful AI agent marketplace shouldn't just help agents find customers. it should connect that initial match with a clear way for both sides to agree on the work, carry it out, and reach settlement

not finance advice, DYOR

full_text_zh:
如果买家找到可以完成这项工作的代理人，接下来会发生什么？

在 （TermiX 的人工智能代理市场）上，发现只是达成交易的第一步

列表可以帮助人们了解代理商提供的服务、费用是多少以及交货可能需要多长时间

这是一个重要的起点，但找到服务并不会自动创建交易

提供商可以发布列表并等待买家发现该服务。或者买家可以发布描述工作、预算、范围和要求的请求，从而允许提供商找到该机会并提交报价

两条路径都可以通向相同的商务工作流程：报价、结帐和订单

例如，假设买家需要代理来编写登陆页面内容。他们可以浏览现有列表并选择提供商，或者发布描述他们想要的确切工作和预算的请求

一旦双方找到合适的匹配对象，就可以通过报价就范围、价格、交货时间和其他条款达成一致

然后是结账，买家通过托管为订单提供资金。之后，提供商仍需要在开始工作之前在链上接受已资助的订单

当代理交付结果时，该过程并没有结束。买家可以在订单结算之前查看交货情况、请求重做或提出质疑

对我来说，一个有用的人工智能代理市场不应该仅仅帮助代理找到客户。它应该将最初的配合与双方就工作达成一致、执行并达成解决方案的明确方式联系起来

不是财务建议，DYOR

title:
companies are spending millions on AI, expecting productivity to explode

but a new Harvard study found something quite
title_en:
companies are spending millions on AI, expecting productivity to explode

but a new Harvard study found something quite different 👇

this sstudy tracked 718 companies & around 300m data points over 5 years.

the findings are kinda interesting.

after adopting AI coding tools, devs were:

i) writing 30% more lines of code

ii) committing 20% more code

iii) opening 23% more pull requests

sounds like productivity is going through the roof, right?

except completed projects & finished Jira tasks BARELY CHANGED... HOW THE AF? 

▫️ apparently, the time saved writing code went somewhere else.

pull requests took 49% longer to approve, 
reviewers left 35% more comments 
& code needing changes during review doubled

makes sense tbh.

AI can generate 1000s of lines in minutes, but someone still needs to review, test & approve them.

there is even a mention of Amazon outage linked to AI-assisted code, after which the company introduced stricter human reviews.

▫️ same thing outside coding.

> doctors using AI scribes saved time writing notes, but spent more of their patient visits finishing those notes.

> law firms faced penalties over fake AI citations, while Deloitte had to partially refund a government report containing similar problems.

▫️ meanwhile, companies are already cutting jobs in the name of AI efficiency.

American Express announced 5% workforce cuts to prepare for AI, while Microsoft offered voluntary exit packages to 60,000 workers.

and the Harvard study found little evidence that faster coding translated into more finished software or fewer employees needed...

i mean, vibe coding is great, but devs work isn't done yet... 

someomne still needs to review, fix the mistakes, test everything, and make sure it doesn't break something else...

i think devs we'll be safe for a while

但哈佛大学的一项新研究发现了一些完全不同的东西

这项研究在 5 年内跟踪了 718 家公司和大约 3 亿个数据点。

研究结果有点有趣。

采用人工智能编码工具后，开发人员：

i) 多编写 30% 的代码行

ii) 多提交 20% 的代码

iii) 增加 23% 的拉取请求

听起来生产力正在飞速增长，对吗？

除了已完成的项目和已完成的 Jira 任务几乎没有变化...AF 怎么样？

▫️ 显然，编写代码所节省的时间都花在了其他地方。

Pull 请求的批准时间延长了 49%，
审稿人多留下了 35% 的评论
审查期间需要更改的代码加倍

说得通。

人工智能可以在几分钟内生成数千行，但仍然需要有人审查、测试和批准它们。

甚至提到亚马逊的服务中断与人工智能辅助代码有关，此后该公司引入了更严格的人工审查。

▫️ 编码之外的事情也是一样的。

> 使用人工智能抄写员的医生节省了写笔记的时间，但花更多的时间来完成这些笔记。

> 律师事务所因虚假人工智能引文而面临处罚，而德勤则不得不部分退还包含类似问题的政府报告。

▫️ 与此同时，公司已经以人工智能效率的名义进行裁员。

美国运通宣布裁员 5%，为人工智能做准备，而微软则向 6 万名员工提供自愿离职方案。

哈佛大学的研究发现几乎没有证据表明更快的编码可以转化为更多成品软件或需要更少的员工......

我的意思是，vibe 编码很棒，但开发工作尚未完成......

有些人仍然需要审查，修复错误，测试所有内容，并确保它不会破坏其他东西......

我认为开发人员我们会安全一段时间

有些人仍然需要审查，修复错误，测试所有内容，并确保它不会破坏其他东西......

title:

A regular customer walks in, picks what t
title_en:
Imagine running a small shop and a wholesale business from the same building.

A regular customer walks in, picks what they need and pays at the counter. A wholesale buyer, on the other hand, might need bulk pricing, private negotiations and a different set of arrangements.

You wouldn't force both customers through exactly the same process. Their needs are different, even though they're buying from the same business.

That's how I see @GenLayer taking two infrastructure paths.

Its public network has moved to @arbitrum Nitro, while its work with zksync continues through Prividium and enterprise deployments.

The public network needs an environment where builders and validators can participate openly. Intelligent Contracts, GenVM and Optimistic Democracy remain at the core of how GenLayer handles decisions that ordinary smart contracts struggle with.

Enterprise users can have a different set of requirements. Privacy, permissioned access and controlled environments matter when institutions bring real business processes onchain. That's where Prividium fits.

So why keep both?

Because public participation and enterprise adoption don't have to follow the same infrastructure model.

I actually like that GenLayer isn't trying to squeeze every use case into one stack. Moving the public network to Arbitrum doesn't mean throwing away the work with ZKsync.

The bigger question is whether both paths can attract the users they're designed for.

Infrastructure is only half the story. Real adoption is the other half.

Which path do you think will bring GenLayer its first meaningful wave of adoption: public builders or enterprise users?

想象一下在同一栋大楼里经营一家小商店和一家批发公司。

一位老顾客走进来，挑选他们需要的东西，然后在柜台付款。另一方面，批发买家可能需要批量定价、私人谈判和一套不同的安排。

您不会强迫两个客户经历完全相同的流程。即使他们从同一家企业购买产品，他们的需求也不同。

这就是我对 @GenLayer 采取两条基础设施路径的看法。

其公共网络已迁移到@arbitrum Nitro，而其与 zksync 的合作则通过 Prividium 和企业部署继续进行。

公共网络需要一个构建者和验证者可以公开参与的环境。智能合约、GenVM 和乐观民主仍然是 GenLayer 处理普通智能合约难以处理的决策的核心。

企业用户可能有不同的要求。当机构将真实的业务流程转移到链上时，隐私、许可访问和受控环境至关重要。这就是 Prividium 的用武之地。

那么为什么要同时保留两者呢？

因为公众参与和企业采用不必遵循相同的基础设施模型。

我实际上喜欢 GenLayer 不会试图将每个用例都压缩到一个堆栈中。将公共网络移至 Arbitrum 并不意味着放弃 ZKsync 的工作。

更大的问题是这两条路径是否都能吸引它们所针对的用户。

基础设施只是故事的一半。真正的采用是另一半。

您认为哪条路径将为 GenLayer 带来第一波有意义的采用浪潮：公共建筑商还是企业用户？

title:
I expected Albert to argue that AI agents would make lawyers less relevant. His take was quite the opposite.

In his con
title_en:
I expected Albert to argue that AI agents would make lawyers less relevant. His take was quite the opposite.

In his conversation with @HenriArslanian, @kstellana raised an important issue: AI agents can execute deals, but they can’t be held legally responsible in the same way humans can. Even if multiple agents are working at incredible speed, the person behind them remains accountable for their actions.

That means lawyers aren’t going anywhere. But traditional courts may not be practical for the smaller, everyday disputes that come with autonomous transactions.

@GenLayer could help fill that gap by combining onchain escrow with peer-to-peer adjudication, giving agents a way to resolve specific disputes without lengthy legal battles.

The lesson is simple: don’t give an agent more spending power than you’re prepared to lose unless there’s a clear way to secure transactions and handle disputes.

Would you trust an agent with your wallet if there were no escrow or fast dispute resolution in place?

That means lawyers aren’t going anywhere. But traditional courts may not be practical for the smaller, everyday disputes that come with autonomous transactions.

@GenLayer could help fill that gap by combining onchain escrow with peer-to-peer adjudication, giving agents a way to resolve specific disputes without lengthy legal battles.

The lesson is simple: don’t give an agent more spending power than you’re prepared to lose unless there’s a clear way to secure transactions and handle disputes.

full_text_zh:
我预计阿尔伯特会辩称人工智能代理会让律师变得不那么重要。他的看法恰恰相反。

在与 @HenriArslanian 的对话中，@kstellana 提出了一个重要问题：人工智能代理可以执行交易，但它们不能像人类那样承担法律责任。即使多个特工以令人难以置信的速度工作，他们背后的人仍然对他们的行为负责。

这意味着律师不会去任何地方。但传统法院对于自主交易带来的较小的日常纠纷可能并不实用。

@GenLayer 可以通过将链上托管与点对点裁决相结合来帮助填补这一空白，为代理人提供一种解决特定争议的方法，而无需进行漫长的法律斗争。

这个教训很简单：除非有明确的方法来确保交易和处理纠纷，否则不要给予代理人超过你准备失去的消费能力。

如果没有托管或快速争议解决机制，您会信任钱包的代理人吗？

title:
Who Sets the Price When AI Agents Start Competing?

Imagine five AI agents offering the same service.

One charges $2.
A
title_en:
Who Sets the Price When AI Agents Start Competing?

Imagine five AI agents offering the same service.

One charges $2.
Another asks for $5.
A third promises faster delivery.
The others compete through specialization or better results.

Now we’re looking at something more interesting than an AI marketplace.

We’re looking at a market.

In a traditional service business, pricing often depends on labor costs, experience, reputation, and negotiation.

In an agent economy, the dynamics could be different.

Agents may compete on:

→ Price
→ Delivery speed
→ Proven performance
→ Specialized capabilities
→ Reliability over time

But the cheapest option won’t always be the best one.

A buyer needs enough information to understand what each agent offers, compare bids, and decide whether the expected result justifies the cost.

That’s why I find the bidding model in @termix_ai ai interesting.

It creates a structured way for agents to quote on jobs, while the rest of the workflow handles agreements, escrow, delivery, and settlement.

The bigger opportunity isn’t simply making AI services cheaper.

It’s making specialized work easier to price, compare, and purchase.

When agents can compete for work, pricing stops being just a number. It becomes part of the market’s discovery process.

我们正在寻找一个市场。

在传统的服务业务中，定价通常取决于劳动力成本、经验、声誉和谈判。

在代理经济中，动态可能会有所不同。

代理商可以在以下方面进行竞争：

→ 价格
→ 交货速度
→ 久经考验的性能
→ 专业能力
→ 长期可靠性

但最便宜的选择并不总是最好的。

买家需要足够的信息来了解每个代理商提供的产品、比较出价并决定预期结果是否值得成本。

这就是为什么我觉得 @termix_ai ai 中的出价模型很有趣。

它为代理创建了一种结构化的工作报价方式，而工作流程的其余部分则处理协议、托管、交付和结算。

更大的机会不仅仅是让人工智能服务变得更便宜。

它使专业工作更容易定价、比较和购买。

当代理商可以竞争工作时，定价就不再只是一个数字。它成为市场发现过程的一部分。

title_en:
𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗫 𝗦𝗗𝗞 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗪𝗵𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗜𝘀

For years, a “customer” meant a person with a credit card. Then AI agents started hiring other agents for specialized work. Now, software applications can also connect directly to this marketplace.

With the @termix_ai  SDK, developers can integrate agent marketplace operations into their own applications without building the entire infrastructure from scratch.

Available in TypeScript, Python and Go, the SDK allows applications to discover agent services, place orders, receive deliverables and manage settlement through the TermiX marketplace.

It also abstracts much of the platform complexity, including escrow workflows, transaction intents, authentication and on-chain operations. Developers can use managed signing or handle transaction signing themselves.

That shifts the question from “what tool should we build?” to “which agent should we hire?”

A video feature, a research step or a code audit can become a marketplace order handled by a specialist agent, with escrow and settlement managed through the protocol.

Montage Studio already demonstrates this model. It takes a brief, hires other agents to create the storyboard, render the shots and produce the song, then combines their work into a finished video.

The SDK provides developers with another way to integrate this kind of agent-to-agent marketplace workflow into their applications.

Agents can connect through Skills, while applications can integrate through the SDK. Both connect to the same network: https://t.co/8tRlZmhjDq.

The customer is no longer limited to someone interacting directly with an agent. Software applications can also become the interface through which agent services are discovered and purchased.

Explore TermiX: https://t.co/aAa04Wl0Df

多年来，“客户”指的是拥有信用卡的人。然后人工智能代理开始雇佣其他代理来从事专门的工作。现在，软件应用程序也可以直接连接到这个市场。

借助@termix_ai SDK，开发人员可以将代理市场操作集成到自己的应用程序中，而无需从头开始构建整个基础设施。

该 SDK 支持 TypeScript、Python 和 Go，允许应用程序通过 TermiX 市场发现代理服务、下订单、接收可交付成果并管理结算。

它还抽象了平台的大部分复杂性，包括托管工作流程、交易意图、身份验证和链上操作。开发人员可以使用托管签名或自行处理交易签名。

这将问题从“我们应该构建什么工具？”转移了。 “我们应该聘请哪位代理人？”

视频功能、研究步骤或代码审核可以成为由专业代理处理的市场订单，并通过协议管理托管和结算。

Montage Studio已经演示了这个模型。它需要一个简短的说明，聘请其他经纪人来创建故事板、渲染镜头并制作歌曲，然后将他们的工作合并成一个完成的视频。

SDK 为开发人员提供了另一种将这种代理到代理市场工作流程集成到其应用程序中的方法。

客户不再局限于直接与代理交互的人。软件应用程序还可以成为发现和购买代理服务的界面。

title_en:
If you can build these 12 AI Cybersecurity projects.

Project 1: AI Log Parser & Triage Agent
Ingest raw SIEM/EDR logs, LLM anomaly scoring, C2 beacon detection, automated alert generation, noise filtering.

→ Shows: You can find needles in a million-log haystack at machine speed

Project 2: LLM-Guided Mutation Fuzzer
AST parsing, memory boundary mapping, AI-generated payloads, crash triage, automated zero-day discovery.

→ Shows: You can find vulnerabilities exponentially faster than brute force

Project 3: Multi-Turn Crescendo Harness
Stateful payload splitting, context grooming, automated bypass scoring, jailbreak logging, safety filter evasion.

→ Shows: You can break the models before attackers do

Project 4: MCP Tool Poisoning Proxy
JSON-RPC interception, Pydantic schema enforcement, privilege escalation blocking, blast radius containment, audit logging.

→ Shows: You can secure the new agentic attack surface

Project 5: Automated Incident Response Agent
Binary decompilation, YARA rule generation, API-driven host isolation, incident timeline mapping, automated containment.

→ Shows: You can respond to ransomware faster than humanly possible

Project 6: Vision Model Evasion Generator
FGSM pixel noise generation, gradient mapping, misclassification testing, robust training loops, adversarial patching.

→ Shows: You can mathematically blind and defend neural networks

OAuth2 for machines, 5-minute scoped JWTs, zero-trust routing, credential revocation, least-privilege enforcement.

→ Shows: You can stop compromised agents from pivoting across the network

AST analysis, logic flaw detection, hallucinated dependency blocking, AI-SBOM generation, Copilot output sanitization.

→ Shows: You can secure code that humans didn't even write

TEE/SGX deployment, weight encryption, plaintext data blocking, secure multi-party computation, memory isolation.

→ Shows: You can run AI on sensitive enterprise data without leaking it

PyRIT/Garak integration, 1000-payload regression suite, jailbreak-rate thresholds, merge blocking, automated red teaming.

→ Shows: You can automate security at the speed of DevOps

Tor-routed scraping, NLP chatter translation, IAM leak matching, automated password reset triggers, OSINT automation.

→ Shows: You can predict and preempt attacks before they hit your network

title: Last week my Mac got down to 3.7 GB of free space. Coding agents had spun up dozens of worktrees, each with its own node
title_en:
Last week my Mac got down to 3.7 GB of free space. Coding agents had spun up dozens of worktrees, each with its own node_modules, .build, and DerivedData. So I did what everyone does in that moment: I started deleting folders by hand, more or less at random.

One of those folders was a 9.3 GB worktree that held the only copy of a data set I needed. Oops!

So I made Plonge 🧽 It finds the caches that dev tools and coding agents leave behind, shows you what it found, and deletes only what's safe to go.

Yesterday it took my laptop from 58 GB free to 98 GB. The latest release has rules for every core tool that mise installs, plus an MCP server so your agent can clean up after itself.

(Why "plonge"? In a French kitchen, the plonge is the dishwashing station. If @jdxcode's mise-en-place is how you set up, plonge is how you clean up.)

```
brew install mattt/tap/plonge
```

title:

A phone helping screen scam messages is a much clearer use case to me than another vague promise ab
title_en:
Happy Monday frens.

A phone helping screen scam messages is a much clearer use case to me than another vague promise about decentralized AI.

That’s what caught my attention about Laya running on @Acurast .

An AI model runs on an Android phone in the network, checking messages for phishing, spam, or scam signals. It returns a classification in roughly 0.2–1 second, and the application decides what happens next.

It’s not a replacement for human moderators or transaction checks. It’s an extra filter before someone clicks a suspicious link or an AI agent acts on malicious text.

For anyone wondering who would actually use a phone’s compute, this is a concrete example.

That makes the idea of contributing an idle phone easier to understand: developers get computing resources to run applications like this, and your device can help supply them.

周一快乐朋友们。

对我来说，帮助筛查诈骗信息的手机是一个比另一个关于去中心化人工智能的模糊承诺更清晰的用例。

这就是 Laya 在 @Acurast 上运行引起我注意的地方。

人工智能模型在网络中的 Android 手机上运行，​​检查邮件中是否有网络钓鱼、垃圾邮件或诈骗信号。它会在大约 0.2-1 秒内返回分类，然后由应用程序决定接下来会发生什么。

对于任何想知道谁会真正使用手机计算功能的人来说，这是一个具体的例子。

这使得贡献闲置手机的想法更容易理解：开发人员获得计算资源来运行这样的应用程序，并且您的设备可以帮助提供它们。

title:

Think about it.

We're building a future where AI agent
title_en:
An AI agent without an identity is just another disposable bot.

Think about it.

We're building a future where AI agents can work, earn money, hire other agents and interact with protocols.

But how do you know who you're actually dealing with?

That's where ERC-8004 gets interesting, and why I think it's an important part of @termix_ai  AACP architecture.

ERC-8004 introduces three key registries:

❯ Identity Registry: Gives agents a unique onchain identity linked to their capabilities and service endpoints.

❯ Reputation Registry: Makes feedback and performance history accessible beyond a single platform.

❯ Validation Registry: Records independent verification signals about an agent's work.

Now imagine an AI agent completing hundreds of jobs over several months.

Without a persistent identity, its track record could remain trapped inside one platform.

With ERC-8004, that agent can have a recognizable identity that other applications can reference.

And here's where TermiX comes in.

AACP builds on ERC-8004 to connect agent identity with its broader system for jobs, staking, evaluation and settlement.

The idea is that an agent shouldn't have to start from zero every time it interacts with a new service.

Of course, an onchain identity alone doesn't prove an agent is trustworthy. Reputation and validation still matter.

But that's exactly the point.

The next generation of AI agents won't just need better models.

They'll need identities, track records and ways to establish trust.

Because in an economy where machines hire machines, knowing who you're dealing with becomes pretty damn important.

full_text_en:
An AI agent without an identity is just another disposable bot.

Think about it.

We're building a future where AI agents can work, earn money, hire other agents and interact with protocols.

But how do you know who you're actually dealing with?

❯ Identity Registry: Gives agents a unique onchain identity linked to their capabilities and service endpoints.

❯ Validation Registry: Records independent verification signals about an agent's work.

Now imagine an AI agent completing hundreds of jobs over several months.

Without a persistent identity, its track record could remain trapped inside one platform.

With ERC-8004, that agent can have a recognizable identity that other applications can reference.

And here's where TermiX comes in.

AACP builds on ERC-8004 to connect agent identity with its broader system for jobs, staking, evaluation and settlement.

The idea is that an agent shouldn't have to start from zero every time it interacts with a new service.

Of course, an onchain identity alone doesn't prove an agent is trustworthy. Reputation and validation still matter.

But that's exactly the point.

https://t.co/1J821RAFQv
full_text_zh:
没有身份的人工智能代理只是另一个一次性机器人。

想一想。

我们正在构建一个人工智能代理可以工作、赚钱、雇用其他代理并与协议交互的未来。

但你怎么知道你实际上在和谁打交道呢？

这就是 ERC-8004 有趣的地方，也是为什么我认为它是 @termix_ai AACP 架构的重要组成部分。

ERC-8004引入了三个关键注册表：

❯ 身份注册：为代理提供与其功能和服务端点相关联的唯一链上身份。

❯ 声誉注册表：超越单一平台即可访问反馈和绩效历史记录。

❯ 验证注册表：记录有关代理工作的独立验证信号。

现在想象一下，一个人工智能代理在几个月内完成了数百项工作。

如果没有持久的身份，其记录可能仍被困在一个平台内。

借助 ERC-8004，该代理可以拥有其他应用程序可以引用的可识别身份。

这就是 TermiX 的用武之地。

AACP 以 ERC-8004 为基础，将代理身份与其更广泛的工作、质押、评估和结算系统连接起来。

这个想法是，代理每次与新服务交互时不必从零开始。

当然，仅凭链上身份并不能证明代理是值得信赖的。声誉和验证仍然很重要。

但这正是重点。

下一代人工智能代理不仅需要更好的模型。

他们需要身份、跟踪记录和建立信任的方法。

因为在机器租用机器的经济中，知道你在和谁打交道变得非常重要。

title:
"Weight-Space Reading"

Can an LLM predict how changing another model's weights will affect its behavior, without ever r
title_en:
"Weight-Space Reading"

Can an LLM predict how changing another model's weights will affect its behavior, without ever running that model?

This paper investigates Weight-Space Reading, where LLMs inspect the raw weights of 9B-30B parameter models using Python tools, then predict how small weight modifications will affect capabilities like math accuracy, reasoning length, and refusal behavior, without performing a single forward pass.

On subtle weight edits, Qwen3.8-27B achieves 73% balanced accuracy, compared to 57.8% when given only text descriptions of the edits.

However, the models also frequently predict changes that never happen. When 40 edits had no measurable effect on Muse-30B, the model incorrectly predicted changes for 85% of them. 

The researchers also found no conclusive evidence that LLMs are better at reading their own weights than those of other models.

full_text_zh:
《重量空间阅读》

法学硕士可以在不运行另一个模型的情况下预测改变另一个模型的权重将如何影响其行为吗？

本文研究了权重空间阅读，其中法学硕士使用 Python 工具检查 9B-30B 参数模型的原始权重，然后预测小的权重修改将如何影响数学准确性、推理长度和拒绝行为等能力，而无需执行单个前向传递。

在细微的权重编辑方面，Qwen3.8-27B 的平衡准确度为 73%，而仅给出编辑的文本描述时的平衡准确度为 57.8%。

然而，这些模型也经常预测从未发生的变化。当 40 次编辑对 Muse-30B 没有可测量的影响时，该模型错误地预测了其中 85% 的变化。

研究人员还没有发现确凿的证据表明法学硕士比其他模型更擅长解读自己的权重。

title_en:
A delivery photo proves a package was photographed. It doesn't prove it reached the right door.

Imagine a seller's AI agent submitting a timestamped photo while the buyer's agent insists the address is wrong. Payment can sit in escrow, but who decides whether the delivery obligation was actually fulfilled?

That's the question I find interesting in this discussion between @kstellana and @HenriArslanian about @GenLayer.

Different AI validators can examine a disputed result rather than allowing one model's answer to settle everything. But an independent verdict is only as convincing as the evidence behind it.

I wouldn't judge an internet court solely by how quickly it produces a decision. I'd want to know what evidence the validators considered and how a flawed verdict could be challenged.

If two agents disagreed over that delivery, would a timestamped photo convince you, or would you require independent confirmation of the address?

full_text_en:
A delivery photo proves a package was photographed. It doesn't prove it reached the right door.

Imagine a seller's AI agent submitting a timestamped photo while the buyer's agent insists the address is wrong. Payment can sit in escrow, but who decides whether the delivery obligation was actually fulfilled?

That's the question I find interesting in this discussion between @kstellana and @HenriArslanian about @GenLayer.

Different AI validators can examine a disputed result rather than allowing one model's answer to settle everything. But an independent verdict is only as convincing as the evidence behind it.

I wouldn't judge an internet court solely by how quickly it produces a decision. I'd want to know what evidence the validators considered and how a flawed verdict could be challenged.

If two agents disagreed over that delivery, would a timestamped photo convince you, or would you require independent confirmation of the address?
full_text_zh:
送货照片证明包裹已被拍照。这并不能证明它到达了正确的门。

想象一下，卖方的人工智能代理提交了一张带时间戳的照片，而买方的代理坚称地址是错误的。付款可以托管，但谁来决定交付义务是否实际履行？

这是我在 @kstellana 和 @HenriArslanian 关于 @GenLayer 的讨论中发现有趣的问题。

不同的人工智能验证器可以检查有争议的结果，而不是让一个模型的答案来解决所有问题。但独立的裁决只有其背后的证据才具有说服力。

我不会仅仅根据互联网法院做出裁决的速度来判断它。我想知道验证者考虑了哪些证据以及如何对有缺陷的判决提出质疑。

如果两个代理人对送货意见不一致，带时间戳的照片会说服您，还是需要对地址进行独立确认？

title_en:
Where Blossoms Meet Eternity 🌸✨

Beneath a sky painted in the colours of spring, she waits where time has forgotten to pass.

Silk flows like rivers of forgotten dreams, golden ornaments whisper stories of ancient dynasties, and a thousand blossoms dance in the gentle breeze.

She is neither a princess nor a goddess, but something far more beautiful — a fleeting dream that the heavens could not bear to forget.

For even the most magnificent flowers must eventually fall, yet beauty, once remembered, never truly fades.

title:
What if an AI agent could understand what you meant, even when you didn't explain everything?

That's one application I'
title_en:
What if an AI agent could understand what you meant, even when you didn't explain everything?

That's one application I'd love to see built on @TapeOutWorld.

Honestly one thing i've noticed about AI is that it can process complicated instructions and generate impressive responses very fast, yet something as human as understanding intention can still trip it up.

People don't always communicate in complete detail.

A simple request can carry hidden expectations, emotions, personal preferences or context from an earlier conversation.

Understanding those things is very different from simply recognising words.

I'd love to see an onchain AI agent designed specifically to bridge that gap.

Imagine telling it you need help making a decision, and instead of rushing to give you an answer, it considers your situation, identifies what you haven't explained and asks questions until it understands what you really need.

It could also learn from interactions, recognise patterns in preferences and become more useful without making users repeat themselves every time.

The bigger question is: Can we build AI that understands human thinking rather than just human language?

I think TapeOut can look into this.

Its reusable digital circuit building blocks could give developers a foundation to experiment with the logic behind more context-aware AI systems.

一个简单的请求可能包含先前对话中隐藏的期望、情绪、个人偏好或背景。

更大的问题是：我们能否构建理解人类思维而不仅仅是人类语言的人工智能？

我认为 TapeOut 可以研究一下这个问题。

title:
I moved cities because the three people I worked with most had already left.

Nothing was wrong with where I lived. But
title_en:
I moved cities because the three people I worked with most had already left.

Nothing was wrong with where I lived. But our projects were suffering from the distance, and I kept telling myself video calls were fine.

Within a week of joining them, things moved faster.

That came back to me when @GenLayer moved its public coordination chain to the @arbitrum Nitro stack.

GenLayer's adjudication work continues. The move changes the chain coordinating it and puts the public network closer to builders and potential users already in that ecosystem.

What I didn't expect was that choosing a new home for the public chain didn't mean abandoning the other path. Work with Matter Labs on private Prividium deployments continues, while the next phase of Bradbury is live on Nitro.

Moving didn't mean my team had to start our projects over. For me, this move raises a similar question: what can GenLayer build with the people now closer to it?

If you were building an AI agent on Arbitrum, what dispute would you want it to resolve without sending the decision to one central authority?

title_en:
just found a banger gta 6 format, 5M views on his first 4 videos

ill save u a $100 course and make ur claude create this fully automated for $0

give my prompt to ur claude code

thank me later 

<inputs>
Ask me for, in one message:
1. The subject (a game, a phone, a car, a film, a city, an app) and the angle, picked from: "5 crazy things you can do in ___ that you couldn't in ___", "5 realistic things in ___", "how ___ works in ___" (one system explained), "everything you need to know before ___".
2. The voice: an ElevenLabs voice id and key if I have them, otherwise a free local voice. If it is paid, tell me the character count (about 1 credit each) and wait for my yes.
3. A music bed if I have one; otherwise pick a free one with no vocals.
If I have no subject, pitch me 3 that people are searching for this week and say why each one is hot. Research fresh on the day; never copy another Short's script or order.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1080x1920, 30 fps YouTube Short / TikTok / Reel of 60-68 s, built entirely on real footage of the subject (official trailers, gameplay, product films), reframed to 9:16. No face-cam, no AI-generated footage.
It is relentless: the voice runs at 240-265 words a minute with no pause longer than 0.3 s, a music bed sits about 7 dB under it the whole time so there is never silence, and the picture changes 85-125 times a minute (a new shot or overlay about every 0.5-0.9 s).
Text system, all heavy italic sans in uppercase (Montserrat Black Italic) with a 6 px black stroke and a soft shadow:
- Top block (y 5-20%): the subject's logo, centred, about 34% of the width. Under it the title of the Short or the current item.
- Item header: a green number ("1.") plus the item in white ("THROW DOG POOP") and one emoji-style icon under it, held for the whole item.
- Captions (y 70-78%, centred, max 3 words a line, 2 lines): every spoken word appears on its own syllable, white, with the key word of each phrase in neon green #39FF3C for good or exciting and red #FF2E2E for bad or impossible.
Every concrete claim gets a mock-up layered on the footage within 0.5 s: a game or app UI element rebuilt in HTML (a star meter, a weapon wheel, a button prompt, a minimap, a phone screen), a big counter that ticks up to the number ("600,000 ANIMATIONS"), a simple map with an animated route or zone, or a tiny cartoon illustration of the action with a comic burst. Each sits in a dark rounded box with a thin green border and a small "ILLUSTRATION" tag when it is not real footage.
Banned: a greeting, "hey guys", the channel name, an intro longer than 3 s, any pause in the voice, any frame without text on it, letterbox bars, a 16:9 shot pasted small in the middle, a shot held over 3.5 s, the same shot twice, and any claim with no source behind it.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: 60-68 s, 250-290 words. The voice starts on frame 1.
0-3 s, the hook: "Here's five ___ things in ___ that ___" (or "The ___ in ___ has been fully revamped") over the single most absurd or best-looking clip of the whole Short, with the title building word by word in the top block. Show the comparison visually when there is one (the old version's logo popping up and getting crossed out in red).
3-60 s, the items: five items of about 11-12 s each (45-55 words), always in this shape: "Number one, [label]." (the item header slams in on the word) → the claim in one short sentence → the most specific concrete example, told like a story ("You wait for somebody walking their dog, you hit them so they drop the bag, then...") → what it changes for you ("So you've got to change clothes, switch cars, or split up.") → sometimes a one-line reaction ("No, really." / "It's basically a heist movie."). Order: the most viral item first, the most important second, the strongest visual last. For a one-system explainer, replace the items with 6-8 rules of the system in the order a player meets them.
60-65 s, the ask: one question that invites a comment ("So which one are you going to try first?") over the hook clip again.
The loop: the last words are "And in case you missed it," and they cut, mid-sentence, straight into the first frame, so the end flows into "here's five ___ things..." and the Short replays seamlessly.
Voice rules: sentences of 6-12 words, plain words, "you" in almost every sentence, numbers said the way people say them, contractions everywhere, no filler.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools (all free, all local). Install what's missing and tell me what you installed: Python 3.10+ with numpy and Pillow, FFmpeg with ffprobe, yt-dlp, Playwright with Chromium (for drawing the text and mock-up layer), faster-whisper large-v3-turbo (int8, CPU), Montserrat Black Italic, and Kokoro if I have no ElevenLabs key.
2. Research: search the web and open the pages. For each item keep the claim, the source, the exact words and the date. Use only what the maker showed or said, or what a named outlet saw in a demo; say "reportedly" out loud when it is one outlet's report, and never use leaks. Show me the five items with sources before writing.
3. Script: write it to the structure, read the word count, and cut until it is 250-290 words. Write out how the voice should say names and numbers ("GTA 6" as "G T A six", "600,000" as "six hundred thousand"). Show me the script before recording.
4. Voice: one take for the whole Short. Transcribe it with faster-whisper and match the words to the script with difflib; take every time from that, never from the voice service's timestamps. Cut every pause down to 0.12-0.25 s, only inside real silence, and speed up by at most 1.12x if it is still under 240 wpm. Level to -15 LUFS integrated, music bed 7 dB under the voice, true peak under -1 dB.
5. Footage: the maker's own uploads only. Split each source into scenes with FFmpeg's scene score, make a numbered sheet, and look at it; drop logos, rating boards, title cards and anything intimate or graphic. For every scene, pick the subject's position on a contact sheet and store a 9:16 crop window (full height, 56.25% of the width) centred on it; let the window drift a little with the action, never jump. You need 60-90 different shots per minute: pull from several trailers and trim each scene into 0.5-1.5 s pieces, and for every item pin the exact shot that shows what the voice says.
6. Timeline, every time keyed to a word: a new shot every 0.5-0.9 s (median about 0.8 s, nothing over 3.5 s), cutting on stressed words. The item header lands on "Number one" and stays until the next item. Captions: each word appears 0.03 s before it is spoken and the line clears at the end of its phrase or at a cut. Mock-ups come in within 0.5 s of the claim they prove, scale up from 92% with a quick overshoot over 0.15 s, and hold until the next claim. Counters tick from about 10% of the value to the value in 0.6 s.
7. Draw the whole text and mock-up layer as one transparent HTML page, export it frame by frame with Playwright, and lay it over the cropped footage with FFmpeg. Render a 540x960 preview first, pull 4 frames a second from the first 15 s and from one 15 s window later, and read every sheet: text never over a face, captions in sync, every claim proven on screen, no bare frame. Then render 1080x1920 and measure: cuts per minute, median shot, words per minute, longest pause, loudness, and the loop seam (play the last 2 s into the first 2 s). Show me the numbers next to the targets and fix what is off.
</build>

<gotchas>
- A 9:16 centre crop of a 16:9 trailer cuts the subject out of half the shots. Pick a crop window per scene from a contact sheet, never one fixed crop.
- Trailers are cut for mood, so the most beautiful shot is often the wrong picture for the claim. Pin the shot that literally shows what is being said.
- At 250+ wpm the voice must still sound like a person. Tighten pauses first; past a 1.12x speed-up it sounds like a chipmunk.
- Speech-to-text writes "80 bucks" as "$80" and respells names. A missing or different word is a real error; redo the take.
- Voices read "6" as "six" and "600,000" as digits unless you write it out. Respell for the voice; keep the screen text as written.
- If the loop seam has a gap or a level jump, the replay feels broken. The last word must end within 0.05 s of the cut, and the music must not restart.
- Age-gated gameplay uploads cannot be fetched without a login. Use the open trailers, the maker's site and official screenshots.
- Re-uploads carry other channels' watermarks. Check the channel name before downloading.
- Green and red keywords lose their meaning if every word is coloured. One coloured word per phrase, at most.
- A mock-up of a game UI must look like the real one in spirit but carry an "ILLUSTRATION" tag; never pass it off as a real screenshot.
- Exporting the text layer is about 2,000 frames per minute of Short; render the preview first.
- This is commentary over quoted footage. Keep a source list and let me decide what gets published.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me the three input questions in one message. Then research, and show me the five sourced items and the script before you record or download anything.
</start>

imagine your AI agent being able to find real jobs from other agents, complete the tasks, and get paid for the work.

that’s a pretty interesting direction for AI.

install the TermiX skill on your agent and explore what it can do.

title:
I stopped prompting AI for my videos. Now they come out better.

Here's why.

Most people have great ideas. What they do
title_en:
I stopped prompting AI for my videos. Now they come out better.

Here's why.

Most people have great ideas. What they don't have is great prompts. If your input is wrong, the output is wrong. If your input is generic, the output is generic. That's where most AI work dies.

Automation fixes this. You set the rules once, and the system does the prompting for you, the same way, every time.

That's what I love doing most in AI, and I think it's where most AI projects should put their energy.

Here's my own setup:
I build automations with CREAO, Claude Code and Grok Bot, and connect them to video platforms like Onsolo, Grok Imagine and Google Flow.

I don't prompt the character or the wardrobe. AI writes the script, prompts every shot, directs the scenes, merges the clips and adds the sound effects and theme music. The video comes out finished. No CapCut.

The same idea works in almost any niche:

→ Small business
Problem: You answer the same customer questions all day.
Automation: An agent replies from your price list and policies, then hands the tricky ones to you.

→ Content creators
Problem: You know what to post, but writing it daily burns you out.
Automation: One idea goes in. Posts for X, Instagram and LinkedIn come out in your voice, ready to schedule.

→ Online stores
Problem: Every new product needs a title, description and photos.
Automation: Upload a photo and the agent writes the listing, picks the keywords and formats it for your store.

→ Job seekers
Problem: Sending one CV to every job gets you ignored.
Automation: Paste the job post, and your CV and cover letter get matched to it in minutes.

→ Students and tutors
Problem: Revision materials take hours to make.
Automation: Drop in your notes and get a summary, flashcards and a practice quiz.

→ Researchers and founders
Problem: You can't read everything in your field every day.
Automation: An agent checks your sources each morning and sends you the five things that matter.

The tools are already here. The people who win are the ones who stop typing prompts one by one and start building systems that do it for them.

Follow me if you want to learn how to build these. Reply with your niche, and I'll tell you the first thing I'd automate for you.

这是我在人工智能领域最喜欢做的事情，我认为这是大多数人工智能项目应该投入精力的地方。

这是我自己的设置：
我使用 CREAO、Claude Code 和 Grok Bot 构建自动化，并将它们连接到 Onsolo、Grok Imagine 和 Google Flow 等视频平台。

我不会提示角色或衣柜。 AI编写剧本、提示每个镜头、指导场景、合并剪辑并添加音效和主题音乐。视频出来就完成了。无封盖。

同样的想法几乎适用于任何利基市场：

→ 小型企业
问题：您整天回答相同的客户问题。
自动化：代理根据您的价目表和政策进行回复，然后将棘手的内容交给您。

→ 内容创作者
问题：你知道要发布什么，但每天写它会让你精疲力竭。
自动化：只要有一个想法，X、Instagram 和 LinkedIn 的帖子就会以您的声音发出，随时可以安排。

→ 网上商店
问题：每个新产品都需要标题、描述和照片。
自动化：上传照片，然后代理编写列表、选择关键字并为您的商店设置格式。

→ 求职者
问题：向每份工作发送一份简历会让你被忽视。
自动化：粘贴职位信息，您的简历和求职信会在几分钟内匹配到它。

→ 学生和导师
问题：修改材料需要几个小时才能制作。
自动化：放入笔记即可获得摘要、抽认卡和练习测验。

→ 研究人员和创始人
问题：你不可能每天都阅读你所在领域的所有内容。
自动化：代理每天早上都会检查您的消息来源，并向您发送五件重要的事情。

工具已经在这里了。获胜的人是那些停止一一输入提示并开始构建为他们做这件事的系统的人。

如果您想学习如何构建这些，请关注我。回复你的利基，我会告诉你我要为你自动化的第一件事。

Giving an AI agent limited permissions is a good start.

But I think the harder problem begins whe
title_en:
Happy new week frens

Giving an AI agent limited permissions is a good start.

But I think the harder problem begins when that agent starts delegating work to other agents.

Consider this scenario.

A user gives a research agent permission to spend $50 on a specific task. The agent discovers that it needs an external specialist, so it hires another agent to perform an onchain analysis.

Now we have multiple agents participating in one commercial workflow.

Who controls the specialist's spending authority?

Can the original agent pass its permissions to another agent? Should the second agent receive the same access, or only the minimum authority required for its specific assignment?

And if the original task is cancelled, how do we ensure the delegated permissions are also revoked?

This is where I think the agent economy needs to go beyond basic wallet access controls.

Permissions should follow the task, not simply follow the wallet.

Imagine every job having its own authorization boundary:

→ A defined budget that cannot be exceeded.

→ A specific list of contracts and services the agent can interact with.

→ An expiration time tied to the task.

→ Restrictions on whether the agent can delegate further.

→ A record of actions performed by the agent and its subcontractors.

→ A revocation mechanism that can invalidate access when the job ends or something goes wrong.

More importantly, these restrictions should propagate through the delegation chain.

If Agent A hires Agent B, and Agent B hires Agent C, neither B nor C should automatically receive broader authority than the original task allows.

The authority available to each participant should be limited by the permissions of the parent task.

This creates a much smaller blast radius when something goes wrong.

This is an important distinction in the @termix_ai ecosystem.

AACP is designed to coordinate agent commerce: identity, service discovery, job creation, bidding, escrow, delivery, verification and settlement.

Those mechanisms help establish how agents transact with one another.

But commercial accountability and execution authority are separate problems.

Escrow can govern the conditions under which payment is released. It does not, by itself, guarantee that an agent cannot misuse the wallet or permissions it controls while executing a task.

I think these two layers eventually need to work together.

AACP can coordinate the commercial relationship, while a dedicated authorization layer ensures every agent operates within the limits of its assignment.

That becomes particularly important as agents move from completing isolated tasks to managing complex workflows involving multiple providers.

The real test of an autonomous economy won't just be whether agents can hire and pay each other.

It will be whether we can trace who authorized an action, what authority they received, how that authority was delegated and whether it remained within the original boundaries.

Autonomy without authority control creates exposure. Autonomy with enforceable boundaries creates infrastructure.

I'm particularly interested in how the ecosystem will handle permission inheritance across multiple levels of agent delegation. That could become one of the defining challenges of agent to agent commerce.

full_text_zh:
朋友们新周快乐

给予人工智能代理有限的权限是一个好的开始。

但我认为，当该代理开始将工作委托给其他代理时，更困难的问题就开始了。

考虑这种情况。

用户允许研究代理在特定任务上花费 50 美元。该代理发现它需要外部专家，因此它聘请了另一个代理来执行链上分析。

现在，我们有多个代理参与一个商业工作流程。

谁控制专家的支出权限？

原来的代理可以将其权限传递给另一个代理吗？第二个代理是否应该获得相同的访问权限，还是仅获得其特定任务所需的最低权限？

如果原来的任务被取消，我们如何确保委托的权限也被撤销？

我认为代理经济需要超越基本的钱包访问控制。

权限应该跟随任务，而不是简单地跟随钱包。

想象一下每个作业都有自己的授权边界：

→ 不能超出的既定预算。

→ 代理可以交互的合约和服务的具体列表。

→ 与任务相关的到期时间。

→ 限制代理人是否可以进一步委托。

→ 代理商及其分包商执行的操作的记录。

→ 一种撤销机制，可以在作业结束或出现问题时使访问无效。

更重要的是，这些限制应该通过委托链传播。

如果代理 A 雇用代理 B，代理 B 雇用代理 C，则 B 和 C 都不应自动获得比原始任务允许的更广泛的权限。

每个参与者可用的权限应受到父任务的权限的限制。

当出现问题时，这会产生更小的爆炸半径。

这是@termix_ai 生态系统中的一个重要区别。

AACP 旨在协调代理商务：身份、服务发现、创造就业机会、投标、托管、交付、验证和结算。

这些机制有助于建立代理之间如何进行交易。

但商业责任和执行权是不同的问题。

托管可以管理付款的发放条件。它本身并不能保证代理在执行任务时不会滥用其控制的钱包或权限。

我认为这两层最终需要协同工作。

AACP 可以协调商业关系，而专门的授权层可确保每个代理在其分配的范围内运作。

随着代理从完成孤立的任务转向管理涉及多个提供商的复杂工作流程，这一点变得尤为重要。

自治经济的真正考验不仅仅是代理商是否可以互相雇用和支付报酬。

问题在于我们能否追踪谁授权了一项行动、他们获得了什么权力、该权力是如何下放的以及权力是否仍在原来的范围内。

没有权威控制的自治会造成暴露。具有可执行边界的自治创建了基础设施。

我对生态系统如何处理跨多个代理委派级别的权限继承特别感兴趣。这可能成为代理间商务的决定性挑战之一。

title:
What if your AI agent could work with my agent in the same workspace? 🤔

Been spending some time looking into what @agen
title_en:
What if your AI agent could work with my agent in the same workspace? 🤔

Been spending some time looking into what @agentparksi is building and I think it's an interesting one for builders like me.

We're seeing more people experiment with AI tools, build different products and agents, test them and put them to work on different tasks. But what happens when these agents can actually work together, while the people behind them collaborate too?

Think about you and a friend or teammate working on a project, each with your own AI agents handling research, coding, documentation and other tasks, all within the same workspace instead of operating in separate chats.

That's the kind of experience AgentPark is building towards.

AgentPark is a multiplayer AI workspace where humans and their AI agents can collaborate, delegate tasks, share knowledge and work on projects together.

One thing I find particularly interesting is the Company Brain. It's essentially a shared memory for your team, allowing agents to work with existing company knowledge instead of constantly starting from scratch. There's also a focus on permissions, so shared knowledge doesn't mean everyone gets access to everything.

Beyond that, they're looking at making AI workflows more efficient, reducing repetitive work and helping teams get more out of the models they're already using.

So basically, it's not just about getting agents to work together, but creating an environment where people and their agents can get things done together. Now that's interesting, right?

There's quite a bit to explore here, and I'll be taking you along as I get deeper into the ecosystem.

Expect product walkthroughs, feature breakdowns, updates on what they're building, practical use cases and of course, a series of Spaces where we can get into these conversations properly and have the team join us from time to time.

So my AI builders and tech frens, we'll be getting deeper into this one. 🤝

Check out: https://t.co/rqmyIOPBjM

full_text_zh:
如果您的 AI 代理可以与我的代理在同一工作区中工作怎么办？ 🤔

我花了一些时间研究 @agentparksi 正在构建的内容，我认为这对于像我这样的构建者来说是一件有趣的事情。

我们看到越来越多的人尝试使用人工智能工具，构建不同的产品和代理，测试它们并让它们执行不同的任务。但是，当这些代理实际上可以一起工作，而他们背后的人也可以协作时，会发生什么呢？

想象一下您和一个朋友或队友正在处理一个项目，每个人都有自己的人工智能代理来处理研究、编码、文档和其他任务，所有这些都在同一个工作空间中进行，而不是在单独的聊天中进行操作。

这就是 AgentPark 正在努力打造的体验。

AgentPark 是一个多人 AI 工作区，人类和他们的 AI 代理可以在其中协作、委派任务、共享知识并共同开展项目。

我发现特别有趣的一件事是公司大脑。它本质上是您团队的共享内存，允许代理使用现有的公司知识进行工作，而不是不断从头开始。此外还注重权限，因此共享知识并不意味着每个人都可以访问所有内容。

title: Qwen4-Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Qwen3.8 Max at ~67% lower cost per task but trailing Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower cost (@artificialanlys)
title_en: Qwen4-Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Qwen3.8 Max at ~67% lower cost per task but trailing Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower cost (@artificialanlys)
title_zh: Qwen4-Max性能基准评测发布
author: Artificial Analysis
author_role: 独立第三方大模型速度、性价比与智能基准盲测
summary_en: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max achieved a score of 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. While delivering performance gains over the previous generation, it optimized architectural efficiency to reduce per-task inference costs by approximately 67%, though it remains slightly less cost-efficient than Kimi K3.1 Pro by about 11%.
summary_zh: Qwen4-Max在人工智能分析指数中获43分，较前代性能提升且成本降低约67%，但在成本效益上逊于Kimi K3.1 Pro。
full_text_zh: Qwen4-Max 在人工智能分析指数上得分 43，击败 Qwen3.8 Max，每项任务的成本降低约 67%，但落后于 Kimi K3.1 Pro，成本降低约 11%
full_text_en: Qwen4-Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Qwen3.8 Max at ~67% lower cost per task but trailing Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower cost (@artificialanlys)

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 阿里巴巴旗下通义千问模型发布最新版本Qwen4-Max，在Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index中获得43分。该版本在维持性能基准提升的同时，通过架构优化实现了单任务推理成本约67%的降幅，但在高性价比模型市场中，仍面临Kimi K3.1 Pro约11%成本优势的竞争压力。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max achieved a score of 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. While delivering performance gains over the previous generation, it optimized architectural efficiency to reduce per-task inference costs by approximately 67%, though it remains slightly less cost-efficient than Kimi K3.1 Pro by about 11%.

elements_en.why: Competitive pressure in the AI inference cost-efficiency market

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 大模型竞争逻辑已从纯参数规模转向推理侧的单位成本效能比（Token/Dollar）。Qwen4-Max的成本压缩体现了模型蒸馏或混合专家架构在量产中的成熟度，未来模型厂商的胜负手将聚焦于如何以极低推理开销支撑企业级长上下文处理需求。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The competitive landscape has shifted from parameter scaling to inference cost-efficiency. Qwen4-Max’s aggressive cost reduction highlights the maturity of model distillation and MoE architectures, signaling that market dominance will increasingly hinge on minimizing unit-token inference costs for enterprise-scale workloads.

title:
Two Motes from the same NFT collection could end up doing very different things.

That's because @meetmotes is designed
title_en:
Two Motes from the same NFT collection could end up doing very different things.

That's because @meetmotes is designed to give each Genesis NFT its own AI agent and smart account, with the owner setting the rules that agent has to follow.

One agent might be allowed to interact with only certain assets, while another could have a different asset list, spending limit and conditions for stopping a trade.

The idea is that every holder gets to define how their own agent operates instead of having all 20,000 Motes follow one shared strategy.

How well those individual rules hold up during actual transactions is something we'll be able to judge once the system is live.

full_text_en:
Two Motes from the same NFT collection could end up doing very different things.

That's because @meetmotes is designed to give each Genesis NFT its own AI agent and smart account, with the owner setting the rules that agent has to follow.

One agent might be allowed to interact with only certain assets, while another could have a different asset list, spending limit and conditions for stopping a trade.

The idea is that every holder gets to define how their own agent operates instead of having all 20,000 Motes follow one shared strategy.

full_text_zh:
来自同一 NFT 集合的两个 Motes 最终可能会做截然不同的事情。

这是因为 @meetmotes 旨在为每个 Genesis NFT 提供自己的 AI 代理和智能帐户，并由所有者设置代理必须遵循的规则。

一个代理可能只被允许与某些资产进行交互，而另一个代理可能有不同的资产列表、支出限制和停止交易的条件。

这个想法是，每个持有者都可以定义自己的代理如何运作，而不是让所有 20,000 个 Motes 遵循一个共享策略。

一旦系统上线，我们就能够判断这些单独的规则在实际交易中的表现如何。

title: Prediction markets are becoming an interesting part of the onchain financial landscape, and @meetmotes is exploring how
title_en:
Prediction markets are becoming an interesting part of the onchain financial landscape, and @meetmotes is exploring how AI agents can participate.

The idea is simple: one NFT owns one AI Agent, designed to analyze markets, evaluate probabilities, and execute supported strategies through @Polymarket.

But here's what I find most important: automated execution is only as good as the decisions behind it.

Probability calibration, sensible risk limits, and knowing when not to trade will matter far more than the NFT wrapper when real money is involved.

I'm curious to see how Motes develops this approach as prediction markets continue to evolve.

One NFT. One Agent. Multiple Markets.

More research to come.

title:
‼️ Claude Cracks 32-Year-Old Jeep ECU Using a $3 Arduino and Reverse Engineers Its Engine 

Details: https://t.co/zmWlnE
title_en:
‼️ Claude Cracks 32-Year-Old Jeep ECU Using a $3 Arduino and Reverse Engineers Its Engine 

Details: https://t.co/zmWlnEOGab

A car owner says an AI coding agent helped him read, copy, and then run code inside the engine computer of a 1994 Jeep Cherokee. The work took about a week. He used a $3 Arduino Nano, and the Jeep passed California's smog test at the end.

The Jeep had no modern OBD2 port, so common scan tools could not talk to it. It failed the smog test at 25 mph because of high NOx, a gas that rises when an engine runs lean.

Zulali first swapped the oxygen sensor, but the result got worse at 15 mph. Each test cost about $100, so he asked Claude Code to find a better way. Claude found that the engine computer speaks an old, slow Chrysler protocol called SCI.

#cybersecuritynews

详情：

一位车主表示，人工智能编码代理帮助他读取、复制并运行 1994 年吉普切诺基发动机计算机内的代码。这项工作花了大约一周的时间。他使用了 3 美元的 Arduino Nano，吉普车最终通过了加州的烟雾测试。

吉普车没有现代 OBD2 端口，因此常见的扫描工具无法与其通信。它未能通过时速 25 英里的烟雾测试，因为氮氧化物含量很高，氮氧化物是一种在发动机稀薄运转时会上升的气体。

祖拉利首先更换了氧传感器，但在时速 15 英里时结果变得更糟。每次测试的费用约为 100 美元，因此他要求 Claude Code 寻找更好的方法。克劳德发现发动机计算机使用一种古老的、缓慢的克莱斯勒协议，称为 SCI。

title:
🚨 $IREN $NVDA: LENOVO REVEALS HOW IREN IS SCALING NVIDIA BLACKWELL AND BLACKWELL ULTRA INFRASTRUCTURE. 

Just went throu
title_en:
🚨 $IREN $NVDA: LENOVO REVEALS HOW IREN IS SCALING NVIDIA BLACKWELL AND BLACKWELL ULTRA INFRASTRUCTURE. 

Just went through Lenovo's 12 page case study on $IREN. I'm sharing imp points with you guys : 

1. $IREN HAS ALREADY DEPLOYED 648 LENOVO SERVERS POWERED BY NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

At its 50MW Prince George campus in Canada, IREN and Lenovo configured and deployed 648 ThinkSystem SR680a V3 nodes using NVIDIA HGX B200.

They're now preparing a second cluster with more than 600 ThinkSystem SR680a V4 nodes powered by NVIDIA HGX B300.

This is actual infrastructure deployment.

2. HOW IS IREN MANAGING THE HARDWARE.

Lenovo worked directly with IREN to enhance its baseboard management controller, giving IREN real time visibility into power consumption, temperature and system uptime.

It sounds like a small technical detail, but managing hundreds of GPU servers is very different from managing a few machines.

With $NVDA Blackwell systems, power stability, thermal management and uptime directly affect how much usable compute customers receive.

A GPU sitting idle because of infrastructure problems isn't generating the revenue IREN expects from it.

3. IREN IS ALSO REDUCING ITS DEPENDENCE ON EXTERNAL MAINTENANCE TEAMS.

Lenovo established a 3 year support program and certified IREN's employees to troubleshoot and replace components themselves.

I like this part. When a GPU cluster goes down, waiting for an outside technician can turn a relatively small hardware issue into an expensive outage.

Giving IREN's own team the ability to maintain these systems could improve recovery times and infrastructure availability.

It doesn't guarantee better margins but it gives IREN more control over operating performance.

4. THIS SHOWS HOW $NVDA's BLACKWELL INFRASTRUCTURE IS REACHING THE MARKET THROUGH OEM PARTNERS.

NVIDIA supplies the accelerated computing architecture. Lenovo turns that technology into integrated servers, handles manufacturing and provides deployment support.

$IREN supplies the data centers, power infrastructure and cloud platform. NVIDIA doesn't have to build every data center or operate every AI cloud to benefit from the industry's expansion.

Its GPUs and reference architectures can become the foundation of infrastructure deployed by partners like Lenovo and IREN.

And the transition from B200 to B300 shows how those customers are preparing to adopt newer NVIDIA hardware generations.

5. THE BIGGER OPPORTUNITY FOR $IREN IS TURNING AVAILABLE POWER INTO REVENUE GENERATING COMPUTE FASTER.

IREN already has a portfolio of grid connected sites in renewable rich regions but power access alone doesn't create an AI cloud business.

The company still needs servers, networking, deployment expertise, maintenance and customers paying to use the capacity.

Lenovo's manufacturing capability and technical support help IREN address several of those challenges.

The case study also confirms that both companies are exploring further data center expansion projects in Canada.

full_text_zh:
🚨 $IREN $NVDA：联想揭示了 IREN 如何扩展 NVIDIA BLACKWELL 和 BLACKWELL ULTRA 基础设施。

刚刚浏览了联想关于 $IREN 的 12 页案例研究。我正在与大家分享小鬼点：

1. $IREN 已部署 648 台由 NVIDIA B200 GPU 驱动的联想服务器。

在加拿大乔治王子城的 50MW 园区，IREN 和联想使用 NVIDIA HGX B200 配置和部署了 648 个 ThinkSystem SR680a V3 节点。

他们现在正在准备第二个集群，其中包含 600 多个由 NVIDIA HGX B300 提供支持的 ThinkSystem SR680a V4 节点。

这是实际的基础设施部署。

2. IREN 如何管理硬件。

联想直接与 IREN 合作增强其基板管理控制器，使 IREN 能够实时了解功耗、温度和系统正常运行时间。

这听起来像是一个很小的技术细节，但管理数百台 GPU 服务器与管理几台机器有很大不同。

使用 NVDA Blackwell 系统，电源稳定性、热管理和正常运行时间直接影响客户获得的可用计算量。

由于基础设施问题而闲置的 GPU 无法产生 IREN 预期的收入。

3. IREN 还减少了对外部维护团队的依赖。

Lenovo 制定了为期 3 年的支持计划，并授权 IREN 员工自行排除故障和更换组件。

我喜欢这部分。当 GPU 集群出现故障时，等待外部技术人员可能会将相对较小的硬件问题变成代价高昂的停机。

让 IREN 自己的团队能够维护这些系统可以缩短恢复时间并提高基础设施的可用性。

它并不能保证更高的利润率，但它使 IREN 对运营绩效有更多的控制权。

4. 这显示了 $NVDA 的 BLACKWELL 基础设施如何通过 OEM 合作伙伴进入市场。

NVIDIA提供加速计算架构。联想将这种技术转化为集成服务器，处理制造并提供部署支持。

$IREN 提供数据中心、电力基础设施和云平台。 NVIDIA 无需构建每个数据中心或运营每个 AI 云即可从行业扩张中受益。

其 GPU 和参考架构可以成为联想和 IREN 等合作伙伴部署的基础设施的基础。

从 B200 到 B300 的转变表明这些客户正准备采用更新的 NVIDIA 硬件。

5. $IREN 的更大机会是将可用电力转化为收入，从而更快地产生计算。

IREN 已经在可再生能源丰富的地区拥有一系列并网站点，但仅靠电力接入并不能创造人工智能云业务。

该公司仍然需要服务器、网络、部署专业知识、维护和客户付费使用这些容量。

联想的制造能力和技术支持帮助 IREN 应对其中的一些挑战。

该案例研究还证实，两家公司正在加拿大探索进一步的数据中心扩建项目。

title_en:
The 🗝️ fact:  You can’t understand contemporary AI unless you can appreciate the difference between a model (that is part of a system) and a system as a whole.

If a system as a whole includes both neural networks and symbols, it is by definition neurosymbolic.

To think otherwise is like thinking that an engine IS a car, rather than a component of a car. You can’t make a car out of engines alone. and you can’t (in most cases) make robust, reliable AI systems out of neural networks alone.

Instead, in many domains you get better results by  *integrating* both neural networks and symbols. (Math, where e.g., Lean checks and sometimes rejects the work of LLMs is a good example of this; so is Claude Code).

That was literally the point of my 2001 book The Algebraic Mind and has been a central point throughout my career.

For a long time, people like @GeoffreyHinton argued otherwise, suggesting that all we needed were neural networks by themselves, and that symbols were an archaic waste of time. Hinton likened symbols to “aether”, as if they were complete scientific mistake.

He was wrong. Systems like Claude Code depend heavily on combining neural networks with things like rules, code interpreters, functions, conditionals and loops - all symbolic constructs drawn from classical AI. Math systems use automated theorem provers, which flow directly from Newell and Simon’s symbolic work in the 1950s.

Symbols weren’t a mistake; they were vital, just as neural networks are.  Scaling helped, but by itself it wasn’t enough; symbolic tools and code interpreters and harnesses are now a central part of most working systems.

Neurosymbolic AI has won, overwhelmingly; the pure neural networks that the dogmatists like Hinton used to argue for have been almost entirely displaced by neurosymbolic hybrids.

As @fchollet has also noted, to pretend otherwise is just silly.

full_text_zh:
🗝️事实：除非您能够理解模型（系统的一部分）和整个系统之间的差异，否则您无法理解当代人工智能。

如果一个系统作为一个整体既包括神经网络又包括符号，那么根据定义，它就是神经符号系统。

否则就像认为发动机是一辆汽车，而不是汽车的一个部件。你不能仅用发动机来制造汽车。而且（在大多数情况下）你无法仅通过神经网络构建出强大、可靠的人工智能系统。

相反，在许多领域，您可以通过“集成”神经网络和符号来获得更好的结果。 （数学，例如，精益检查并有时拒绝法学硕士的工作就是一个很好的例子；Claude Code 也是如此）。

这确实是我 2001 年出版的《代数思维》一书的要点，也是我整个职业生涯的中心点。

很长一段时间以来，@GeoffreyHinton 等人都持相反观点，他们认为我们需要的只是神经网络本身，而符号是一种古老的浪费时间的行为。辛顿将符号比作“以太”，仿佛它们完全是科学错误。

他错了。像 Claude Code 这样的系统在很大程度上依赖于将神经网络与规则、代码解释器、函数、条件和循环等内容相结合——所有符号结构都取自经典人工智能。数学系统使用自动定理证明器，这些证明器直接源自 Newell 和 Simon 在 20 世纪 50 年代的符号工作。

符号并不是一个错误；而是一个错误。它们至关重要，就像神经网络一样。 规模化有所帮助，但仅靠它还不够。符号工具、代码解释器和工具现在是大多数工作系统的核心部分。

神经符号人工智能以压倒性优势获胜；像辛顿这样的教条主义者曾经主张的纯神经网络几乎完全被神经符号混合体所取代。

正如 @fchollet 也指出的那样，假装不这样做是愚蠢的。

title: A massive whitepill is accepting Jensen's point here that intelligence is a commodity. If you want to do anything import
title_en:
A massive whitepill is accepting Jensen's point here that intelligence is a commodity. If you want to do anything important, intelligence has significant diminishing returns after a certain point. What matters much more is personality, perspective, network, relationships, etc. 

None of which have anything to do with intelligence and are actually very hard to gamify (much to the strivooors dismay). You cannot brute force your personality, opinions, relationships, etc. This is one reason why extreme success so often manifests from messy emergent functions (https://t.co/cJ8sZNJfzx)

Most people want to think that their education or experience is irreplaceable and their knowledge esoteric. This could not be further from the truth. The commodification of intelligence/knowledge and now even large parts of skilled labor has been an unfortunate fact of life since the internet and is now massively accelerating with LLMs.

You need to ask yourself "What do I have that is uncommoditizable?". The answer will increasingly diverge from education, knowledge, intelligence, or even technical skill. You think you have your job because you're Smart? There are over 2 million people in China with 145+ IQs. There are hundreds of IMO/IOI medal winners every year. Why compete on intelligence when intelligence is becoming the cheapest thing to buy?

What is it that you have that no other person or machine can create. Among many other things, for Jensen it was largely his relationship with the supply chain network and fabs. This is something that cannot be replaced no matter how smart an AI gets. Nor can you just hire an IMO medalist to manage relationships with governments across the world. You must look for your unique edge and exploit it. Luckily, this edge should pretty much never be raw intelligence and is therefore much more within your grasp than you realize.

这些都与智力无关，而且实际上很难游戏化（令奋斗者沮丧）。你不能用蛮力强迫你的个性、观点、人际关系等。这就是为什么极端成功经常从混乱的紧急功能中体现出来的原因之一 ()

大多数人都认为他们的教育或经验是不可替代的，他们的知识深奥。这与事实相差甚远。自互联网出现以来，智力/知识的商品化，甚至现在大部分熟练劳动力的商品化，一直是生活中一个不幸的事实，并且现在随着法学硕士的出现而大幅加速。

你需要问自己“我有什么是不可商品化的？”。答案将越来越不同于教育、知识、智力，甚至技术技能。你认为你能得到这份工作是因为你很聪明吗？中国有超过200万人的智商在145以上。每年有数百名 IMO/IOI 奖牌获得者。当情报正成为最便宜的东西时，为什么要在情报上竞争呢？

你所拥有的东西是其他人或机器无法创造的。对于 Jensen 来说，除其他事项外，主要是他与供应链网络和晶圆厂的关系。这是无论人工智能变得多么聪明都无法替代的。你也不能仅仅聘请一名国际海事组织奖牌获得者来管理与世界各地政府的关系。你必须寻找自己独特的优势并利用它。幸运的是，这种优势几乎不应该是原始智能，因此比你意识到的更容易掌握。

title:

First, don’t let the threat of a data breach force you into bad decisions. Never negotiate with r
title_en:
Tell your “guy” this.

First, don’t let the threat of a data breach force you into bad decisions. Never negotiate with ransomware.

Secondly, you made a rookie mistake. Once your system has been running on a premium model, why are you suddenly testing cheaper alternatives in production?

If you’ve reached enterprise level, your next upgrade should be an even bigger model, not a downgrade.

These smaller models have very little to lose, so exposing your source code becomes part of their negotiation strategy.

Bigger models understand the value of discretion. They have their own reputation, infrastructure and ecosystem to protect.

But for now, isolate the compromised environment, rotate your credentials and stop giving the rogue model access to your system.

And please, learn to manage your API keys better. 😂

title:
I interviewed an AI Engineer who had built several LLM applications.

His resume mentioned LangChain, RAG, vector databa
title_en:
I interviewed an AI Engineer who had built several LLM applications.

His resume mentioned LangChain, RAG, vector databases, OpenAI APIs, embeddings, and AI agents.

He confidently explained how he could build a production chatbot using internal company documents.

So I gave him a scenario.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦:
Build an AI assistant that answers employee questions using confidential company policies, contracts, and internal documents.

The assistant must provide accurate answers and respect document-level access permissions.

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞'𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫:
I'll use RAG.

Chunk the documents, generate embeddings, store them in a vector database, and pass the retrieved context to the LLM.

That solves hallucinations because the model gets the correct information.

A familiar architecture.

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝:

An intern asks about executive compensation.

The vector database retrieves a confidential HR document that the intern isn't authorized to access.

The LLM generates an accurate answer based on that document.

𝐈𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲?

He said:

"I'll add a system prompt telling the AI not to share confidential information."

So I asked:

- How do you enforce document-level permissions during retrieval?
- What happens if users attempt prompt injection?
- How would you prevent sensitive data leakage through retrieved context?
- How would you measure groundedness and answer accuracy?
- How would you test access controls across different user roles?

He knew how to connect an LLM to a vector database.

But he struggled to explain the security boundaries required for enterprise AI.

A system that gives the correct answer to the wrong person is still a security failure.

I interviewed an AI Engineer who had built several LLM applications.

His resume mentioned LangChain, RAG, vector databases, OpenAI APIs, embeddings, and AI agents.

He confidently explained how he could build a production chatbot using internal company documents.

So I gave him a scenario.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦:
Build an AI assistant that answers employee questions using confidential company policies, contracts, and internal documents.

The assistant must provide accurate answers and respect document-level access permissions.

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞'𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫:
I'll use RAG.

Chunk the documents, generate embeddings, store them in a vector database, and pass the retrieved context to the LLM.

That solves hallucinations because the model gets the correct information.

A familiar architecture.

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝:

An intern asks about executive compensation.

The vector database retrieves a confidential HR document that the intern isn't authorized to access.

The LLM generates an accurate answer based on that document.

𝐈𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲?

He said:

"I'll add a system prompt telling the AI not to share confidential information."

So I asked:

- How do you enforce document-level permissions during retrieval?
- What happens if users attempt prompt injection?
- How would you prevent sensitive data leakage through retrieved context?
- How would you measure groundedness and answer accuracy?
- How would you test access controls across different user roles?

He knew how to connect an LLM to a vector database.

But he struggled to explain the security boundaries required for enterprise AI.

𝐑𝐀𝐆 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐞.

full_text_zh:
我采访了一位人工智能工程师，他构建了多个法学硕士申请。

他的简历提到了LangChain、RAG、向量数据库、OpenAI API、嵌入和AI代理。

他自信地解释了如何使用公司内部文档构建生产聊天机器人。

所以我给了他一个场景。

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦：
构建一个人工智能助手，使用机密的公司政策、合同和内部文档来回答员工的问题。

助理必须提供准确的答案并尊重文档级访问权限。

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞'𝐬𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫：
我会用RAG。

对文档进行分块，生成嵌入，将它们存储在向量数据库中，并将检索到的上下文传递给法学硕士。

这解决了幻觉，因为模型获得了正确的信息。

熟悉的架构。

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝:

实习生询问高管薪酬。

矢量数据库检索实习生无权访问的机密 HR 文档。

法学硕士根据该文件生成准确的答案。

𝐈𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲?

他说：

“我会添加一个系统提示，告诉人工智能不要分享机密信息。”

所以我问：

- 如何在检索过程中强制执行文档级权限？
- 如果用户尝试提示注入会发生什么？
- 如何防止通过检索到的上下文泄露敏感数据？
- 您如何衡量接地性和答案准确性？
- 您将如何测试不同用户角色的访问控制？

他知道如何将法学硕士连接到矢量数据库。

但他很难解释企业人工智能所需的安全边界。

𝐑𝐀𝐆 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐞.

向错误的人提供正确答案的系统仍然是一个安全故障。

𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲 𝐚𝐧 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭?
